text:
sam_w: heads up — noticed a sustained tail-latency spike on streaming toolloop runs after the runtime bump this morning. mem keeps climbing during 30+ min sessions (staging). :eyes:

rhea: details? repro steps? is this the longcontext toolchain?

sam_w: yeah longcontext + toolloop. repro: start a 20-step tool loop with repeated function calls and long prefixes, let it run ~30m. observed: KV pages in use climbs steadily, eviction throughput drops, and we get 200-500ms extra per-token latency spikes.

kevin: any heap dumps / pprof? can you paste the hot stacks?

sam_w: pasted a trimmed pprof sample below from the 25m mark (profiler attached to staging runtime). high-level:
```
  40%  runtime::kv::slot_hold_loop
  22%  runtime::storage::pagewalk_eviction
  12%  runtime::scheduler::backoff_sleep
  10%  kernel::select_kernel_for_shard
  8%   tokio::poll::pending_wait
  8%   other small frames
```
kevin: hmm slot_hold_loop up that much smells like something's pinning KV slots and not releasing. could be a refcount regression when toolloop retries aborted requests.

rhea: did anything change in the commit that touched cache pin/unpin paths? last change was the kernel-selection refactor and the batching heuristic tweak.

sam_w: yeah the kernel-selection refactor moved a few hot paths around; also there was a small change in batch commit where we try to pre-pin pages for the next micro-batch.

perf-bot: autometrics snapshot (25m window): 
```
kv_pages_in_use: 1.1M -> 2.0M
evict_ops/sec: 1400 -> 260 (drop)
avg_slot_hold_ms: 3.2 -> 112.4
page_fragmentation_ratio: 0.38 -> 0.67
```
kevin: page_fragmentation_ratio jump + avg_slot_hold_ms aligns with the slot-hold hypothesis. If pre-pin fails mid-batch, we might leave stale holds.

rhea: could also be an ordering problem: if kernel selection now yields a fast path that skips the usual unpin guard, we might leak holds under error paths.

sam_w: reproduced with debug build — found logs showing 'pin acquired but unpin not found' in a few code paths where batch aborts on downstream tool error. sample snippet: 
```text
[11:02:14.321] pin> id=0x7f8c3a lock_count=1
[11:02:14.322] toolloop> downstream error, aborting batch uid=abcd
[11:02:14.322] batch> skipped_unpin path uid=abcd (reason: aborted)
```
kevin: nice catch. so the pre-pin + early-abort path didn't call the unpin. that's probably enough to explain slow evictions and pagewalk pressure.

rhea: plan: 1) add a test that simulates mid-batch abort and asserts refcounts go to zero, 2) add defensive unpin in the abort path, 3) instrument a metric kv.pin_leak_count and kv.slot_hold_time histogram.

sam_w: I'll open a small PR for the defensive unpin and add a staging flag to enable extra KV debug logging. PR will include the unit test and metric wiring. assigning to @kevin for microbench and to @rhea for review.

kevin: I'll run a bisect across the last two runtime builds to confirm which change introduced it, and run the microbench harness for 1hr to watch fragmentation numbers. also will add a short-lived task to periodically walk pinned-pages and log anomalies. :mag:

rhea: if fixes look good, we should backport to the 2.3.x release (this impacts Dedicated customers with long-running toolloops).

sam_w: created a ticket and linked logs / pprof in it: https://redwood.internal/issue/INC-9843 — added pointer to staging dump. will post PR link shortly. thanks y'all. :thumbsup:

kevin: quick mitigation idea — lower pre-pin aggressiveness (disable pre-pin) in config until we ship fix, that should reduce new leaks while we patch.

rhea: agreed. I'll flip the flag in staging and create a runbook note for ops.

sam_w: confirmed flip done. staging shows avg_slot_hold_ms back down to ~4ms after disabling pre-pin. will proceed with PR.

kevin: will schedule a follow-up in #eng-runtime tomorrow to confirm no regressions after the fix.

sam_w: ack, thanks.
